title: A Memory-Augmented LLM Agent for Open-Ended Navigation in MiniGrid
objective: Improve MiniGrid navigation under partial observability through memory-grounded LLM action selection.
description: Developed with Vegim Bytyqi and Pawan Saxena, this project uses gpt-4.1-mini as an action-selection policy for partially observable BabyAI/MiniGrid environments. A Python state layer converts 7×7×3 egocentric observations into compact text, projects visible objects into a persistent spatial map, and tracks visited cells. The LLM receives the mission, local symbolic map, held object and memory-derived subgoal, then selects one discrete action that is validated before execution. An initial 360° scan and repeated-state detection help address looping and wrong-object selection. The paper reports three successful sample runs and one failed run, including both outcomes on UnlockPickup; these examples do not establish an aggregate benchmark success rate. Remaining limitations include pose drift, policy variance and limited long-horizon planning beyond subgoals.
lead: Grounding an LLM navigation policy in persistent spatial memory, a local symbolic map and structured prompts.
cardBlurb: Observe, remember, reason and act: a MiniGrid agent with spatial memory, symbolic maps and validated LLM decisions.

meta.v: Vegim Bytyqi · Nitish Devrani · Pawan Saxena

paperNames: Full paper — A Memory-Augmented LLM Agent
tasks: Combined a Python state-and-memory layer with an LLM policy that selects one discrete action per timestep.
Encoded visible objects, relative offsets, held objects and blocked directions in a stable textual representation.
Grounded decisions in a local symbolic map and generic subgoals such as reaching a key before unlocking a door.
Used bootstrap scanning, visited-cell tracking, repeated-state detection and action validation to limit unproductive loops.
Examined sample runs under runtime and token constraints: successful UnlockPickup, PutNext and KeyInBox episodes took 45, 70 and 50 steps respectively, while a second UnlockPickup run failed.

title: Smart Bike Light Pro
objective: Control bicycle headlight beam states from a forward-facing camera using a lightweight neural network.
description: Developed at UTN with Sagnik Das and Muhid Abid Siddiqui, in collaboration with Supernova GmbH, Smart Bike Light Pro is a vision-based adaptive headlight prototype. An ESP32-CAM streams MJPEG video over Wi-Fi to a Raspberry Pi 5. A lightweight residual CNN predicts off, dim or high beam, and temporal stabilization smooths transitions before GPIO-driven relay control switches the headlight. The model uses policy-derived BDD100K labels based on time of day and hazard bounding boxes. Custom 3D-printed enclosures and bicycle mounts integrate the hardware for on-bike testing. The report records 93.99% classification accuracy on 18,482 BDD100K test images and 20.4 ms model inference on Raspberry Pi 5, with a 10 Hz control loop. The classification result measures agreement with derived labels, not real-world glare safety. On 255 bike-ride segments, the deployment configuration reports 80.8% dimming recall and a 30.6% false-positive rate; twilight, distant hazards and some single-headlight vehicles remain challenging.
lead: Camera-based adaptive headlight control — a lightweight CNN, Raspberry Pi inference and custom bicycle-mounted hardware.
cardBlurb: A camera-to-headlight pipeline that predicts off, dim and high beam on Raspberry Pi 5, housed in custom 3D-printed enclosures.

meta.v: 20.4 ms on Raspberry Pi 5 · 10 Hz control loop

title: How Far Can You Compress CLIP? A Systematic Study of Pruning and Quantization for Edge Deployment
objective: Map the accuracy and compression trade-offs of pruning and quantization in CLIP-family models for edge deployment.
description: A systematic empirical study spanning 300+ experiments on CLIP ViT-B/32, CLIP ViT-B/16 and MobileCLIP-S1. I compared six precision configurations, magnitude and activation-aware Wanda pruning, structured FFN pruning, and EViT token pruning, including both prune-then-quantize and quantize-then-prune orderings. Evaluation covers zero-shot classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and STL-10, with additional full-resolution ImageNette validation and three-seed analysis for key configurations. Wanda preserves substantially more accuracy than magnitude pruning on ViT-based CLIP models, while MobileCLIP-S1 is more resilient at high sparsity. Sub-8-bit quantization is simulated: the study measures its accuracy effects, not realized 4-bit memory savings. Experiments ran on A100 GPUs; on-device latency and energy benchmarking remain future work. Architecture comparisons are also influenced by different pretraining data and recipes.
lead: 300+ experiments exploring how far CLIP-family models can be pruned and quantized while preserving zero-shot accuracy.
cardBlurb: Wanda pruning, 4-bit quantization and pipeline ordering across three CLIP models — mapping accuracy, sparsity and the limits of compression.
paperNames: Full paper — How Far Can You Compress CLIP?
cardTitle: How Far Can You Compress CLIP?
tasks: Designed and ran the compression study, including pipeline ordering, 30–70% sparsity sweeps and three-seed variance analysis.
Implemented activation collection for Wanda calibration using 128 images and 20 text prompts, alongside magnitude, structured FFN and EViT pruning experiments.
Found a 1.39 percentage-point advantage on CIFAR-100 for pruning ViT-B/16 before quantization; ordering differences for MobileCLIP-S1 were within noise.
Validated MobileCLIP-S1 on ImageNette: 99.62% top-1 accuracy with Wanda 30% and simulated 4-bit group-128, compared with 99.67% at FP32.
Distinguished simulated low-bit accuracy from packed storage: unstructured pruning creates sparsity but does not shrink dense model files.

title: Cloud Economics
objective: Analyze and optimize cloud expenditure through automated infrastructure scaling.
description: Investigated the economics of cloud computing — comparing on-premises vs. cloud deployment costs, analyzing pricing models (pay-as-you-go, reserved instances, spot pricing), and evaluating strategies for right-sizing infrastructure. The project includes a detailed report and presentation covering cost optimization frameworks, automated scaling policies, and real-world case studies of cloud migration ROI.

title: Learning Companion App
objective: Help teachers reflect on lessons, review assessments and develop teaching ideas with AI feedback.
description: An end-to-end web application for lesson reflection and AI-assisted teaching, built around Digitales Didaktisches Design (DDD). Teachers can describe and rate a lesson, save a draft, review assessment scores and ask AI follow-up questions. The dashboard brings completed assessments and work in progress together across five dimensions: learning goals, learning activities, assessment and feedback, social learning, and digital technologies. A separate AI group chat helps teachers explore lesson ideas through three perspectives: idea generation, constructive critique and synthesis, with saved conversations available to revisit. The React and TypeScript interface connects to a Node.js and Express server, which manages access and integrates MongoDB for users, lessons and chats, AcademicCloud for AI feedback, and Nodemailer / SMTP for account and support emails.
tasks: Architected and developed the frontend, backend, database and cloud deployment, with ongoing production maintenance.
Built lesson assessment workflows with drafts, results and AI feedback, supported by a dashboard for completed and ongoing assessments.
Integrated AI group conversations with idea-generation, critique and synthesis perspectives, follow-up exchanges and saved chats.
Implemented registration, email confirmation and role-based workflows for teachers, administrators and super administrators.
Provided administration tools for user access, test assessments, AI instructions, health checks and logs; super administrators can assign admin roles and review test assessments.
lead: A workspace for lesson reflection, structured assessments and conversations with AI teaching perspectives.
cardBlurb: Lesson assessments, visual feedback and AI group discussions — a teaching companion built with React, TypeScript and AcademicCloud.

title: Stream Data Pipeline Dashboard
objective: Visualize streaming query metrics, predictions, threshold alerts and user billing in a live Next.js dashboard.
description: Built the real-time Next.js dashboard for Team Stream Dreamers, connecting Kafka-backed query data to the frontend through WebSockets. The team system stores raw data in DuckDB and processes, aggregates and enriches query records for streaming. My primary responsibility was the dashboard: Recharts visualizations for query execution trends, query-type distributions and cluster utilization, alongside per-user resource costs and serverless usage. The interface compares live query counts with predictions, displays threshold alerts and provides access to alert history. To keep frequent updates manageable, charts retain the latest 10 data points, prediction batches are appended every 10 updates, and WebSocket reconnect logic handles connection drops. Improved prediction models, theme switching and support for multiple Kafka topics are described as future enhancements in the report.
tasks: Designed and implemented the real-time Next.js dashboard for Team Stream Dreamers.
Integrated Recharts line and stacked bar charts for query trends, query types and cluster utilization.
Displayed per-user execution costs and serverless usage in billing summaries.
Implemented dynamic threshold alerts that disappear after 5 seconds, with a dropdown for historical alerts.
Limited charts to the latest 10 data points and buffered predictions for insertion every 10 updates.
Added WebSocket reconnect logic to recover from connection drops during frequent updates.
lead: Live query analytics, predictions, alerts and user billing — streamed from Kafka to a Next.js dashboard over WebSockets.
cardBlurb: A live Next.js dashboard for Kafka query metrics, prediction trends, threshold alerts and per-user billing.
